tools.name: run_revenue_check
tools.description: Runs a read-only, from-outside revenue-path teardown of a public website and returns a dollar-proof report. Free and needs no key. It loads the site as a visitor, follows the money path (landing, call to action, lead form, checkout reachability, analytics presence), and reports where revenue is at r

tools.name: get_latest_findings
tools.description: Returns the most recent revenue-path check for a given site, including its dollar-proof findings. Reads an account history, so it needs a Smoke Run API key. Returns an empty result when no check has been run for that site yet.

tools.name: get_money_system
tools.description: Detects the revenue stack a public site runs on (payment processor, CRM or lead destination, email provider, booking tool, analytics and ad pixels) from its public page, and returns the funnel map. Free and needs no key. Each node notes what a connected check can verify end to end.

tools.name: list_checks
tools.description: Lists recent revenue-path checks for the authenticated account, newest first. An optional siteUrl narrows the list to one site.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_money_system · Private data: get_latest_findings · Public sink: get_money_system · Destructive: run_revenue_check, get_latest_findings.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_money_system · Private data: get_latest_findings · Public sink: get_money_system · Destructive: run_revenue_check, get_latest_findings

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
